source: Curated static seed dataset of classic interview problems. LeetCode has no official public API and scraping their GraphQL endpoint is fragile and ToS-gray, so this project ships a curated JSON seed. Python-only. Each problem carries an entry_point (Solution method name), starter_code, and test_cases (args + expected) used by the Python sandbox to run and grade submissions. To expand, add records matching this schema (or point PROBLEMS_PATH at a larger dump).

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.
hints: Use a hash map to store value -> index as you iterate.
For each element, check if target - element is already in the map.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description:
Given a string `s` containing just the characters `'('`, `')'`, `'{'`, `'}'`, `'['` and `']'`, determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if:
1. Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets.
2. Open brackets must be closed in the correct order.
3. Every close bracket has a corresponding open bracket of the same type.
hints: Use a stack. Push opening brackets; on a closing bracket, the top of the stack must be its match.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.description:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`-th day.

You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve. If you cannot achieve any profit, return `0`.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6-1 = 5.
No transactions are done and the max profit = 0.

hints: Track the minimum price seen so far and the best profit achievable at each step.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.description:
Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.

An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Count character frequencies and compare, or sort both strings.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.description:
Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.

Note: for grading, return each group's members sorted, and the list of groups sorted; the sandbox normalizes ordering before comparing.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Use the sorted string (or a character-count tuple) as a hash key to bucket anagrams.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with the length of 3.
The answer is "b", with the length of 1.
The answer is "wke", with the length of 3.

constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.
hints: Use a sliding window with a set/map of last-seen indices; move the left boundary past any repeat.

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all the triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j`, `i != k`, and `j != k`, and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`.

Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets. The sandbox normalizes triplet and list ordering before comparing.

examples.explanation: The only possible triplet does not sum up to 0.

hints: Sort the array, fix one element, then use two pointers for the remaining pair. Skip duplicates.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.description:
Given an `m x n` 2D binary grid `grid` which represents a map of `'1'`s (land) and `'0'`s (water), return the number of islands.

An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically. You may assume all four edges of the grid are all surrounded by water.
hints: Iterate cells; when you find a '1', flood-fill (DFS/BFS) all connected land and count one island.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.description:
You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount` representing a total amount of money.

Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return `-1`.

You may assume that you have an infinite number of each kind of coin.
hints: Bottom-up DP: dp[x] = min coins to make x; dp[x] = min(dp[x - coin] + 1).

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is equal to the product of all the elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`.

You must write an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and without using the division operation.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.
hints: Compute prefix products left-to-right, then multiply by suffix products right-to-left.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.description: Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is `1`, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
hints: Two pointers from both ends; water above each bar is min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i].

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.description:
Given two sorted arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of size `m` and `n` respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays.

The overall run time complexity should be `O(log (m+n))`.
hints: Binary search the partition on the smaller array so left halves <= right halves.
